sections.content:
A **variable** is like a labeled box where you store something so you can use it later. 📦

You create one with `=`. The name goes on the **left**, the value goes on the **right**.

sections.label: Run it — then change 'Alex' to a made-up name!

sections.content:
Notice two kinds of data:

• **`'Alex'`** has quotes → it's a **string** (text)
• **`16`** has no quotes → it's an **integer** (a whole number)

Numbers don't need quotes. If you put quotes around a number, Python treats it as text, not math!

sections.label: Python knows the difference — run this

sections.content:
The **`type()`** function tells you what kind of data something is. `<class 'int'>` means integer, `<class 'str'>` means string.

💡 You can also do math with number variables:

sections.prompt: Create a variable called **`my_name`** with a made-up name, and a variable called **`my_age`** with a made-up age. Then **print both** of them.
sections.starter: # Make your two variables, then print each one
hints: Set them like this: my_name = 'YourName' and my_age = 16
Then use print(my_name) and print(my_age) on separate lines.

check.description: Create my_name (text) and my_age (a whole number), then print both.

tests.message: my_age holds a whole number (an integer — no quotes!)
